metadata.harness: claude -p --model M --effort E --append-system-prompt <blind-scorer agent body> --allowedTools Read,Grep,Glob
metadata.design: Two phases in the order the cost doc prescribes: (1) effort swept on the current model (opus x low/high/xhigh); (2) models swept at a fixed effort (haiku/sonnet/opus/fable x high).
metadata.metrics: NOT score agreement. (a) does the cell preserve the RANKING between skills, (b) is within-cell run-to-run spread below the loop's +2 keep threshold.
metadata.caveats: n=3 per cell is thin; the four skills span 68-86 so ranking stability on closer-quality skills is untested; the metered Sonnet cost run finished early and under-reports.

findings.effort_is_flat: Opus low/high/xhigh: means within ~3 points, no consistent direction, identical rankings, spread medians 2.5/3.0/3.0. Raising scorer effort buys nothing.
findings.frontier_floor_confirmed: At high effort Haiku was the ONLY model to reorder the skills, and swung 14 points across 3 runs of one unchanged skill. Sonnet, Opus and Fable returned identical rankings. Floor holds — on ranking instability and variance, not on the shallow-justification argument.
findings.floor_not_a_pin: Sonnet and Fable both preserve ranking. Fable was steadiest (spread median 2, max 3); Opus harshest.
findings.cross_model_offset: Haiku/Sonnet/Fable all scored ~+5 to +6 above Opus on the same skills. Totals are not comparable across scorer models.
findings.noise_exceeds_keep_threshold: No model held within-cell spread under +/-2 (medians 2-4, maxima 3-6, 14 for Haiku). A bare +2 keep decision is inside measurement error. SKILL.md amended to treat a bare +2 as undecided.
